questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes a data structure?
questions.option_b: A method of organizing and storing data for efficient access and modification

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a linear data structure?
Which of the following is a nonlinear data structure?

questions.option_a: Only the memory address of data
questions.option_c: Data and operations without specifying implementation details

Which data structure is commonly used for Depth-First Search (DFS)?
The postfix form of A + B * C is:
The prefix form of A + B * C is:
The postfix form of (A+B)*C is:
During postfix evaluation, when an operator is encountered, the evaluator generally:
questions.option_a: Pushes the operator onto the stack
questions.option_b: Pops operands, applies the operator, and pushes the result

questions.question_text: In a singly linked list, each node normally contains:
questions.option_a: Data and pointer to the next node
questions.option_d: Pointer to previous and next nodes

questions.question_text: What is the main advantage of a linked list over a fixed-size array?
questions.option_b: Dynamic size and easier insertion/deletion without shifting elements

questions.question_text: Inserting a node at the beginning of a singly linked list requires:
questions.option_b: Updating the new node's next pointer and the head pointer

questions.question_text: In a circular linked list, the next pointer of the last node points to:
A doubly linked list node generally contains:
questions.option_b: Data and two pointers: previous and next

questions.question_text: Which linked list is particularly useful when traversal is required in both directions?

questions.option_c: Coefficient, exponent, and link to the next term
questions.option_d: Only the address of the polynomial

questions.question_text: Which linked-list operation generally requires changing links rather than shifting all subsequent elements?

questions.option_a: It must contain exactly two nodes

questions.question_text: Consider: int stack[5], top = -1; Which statement correctly pushes x?

What is Python?

questions.option_a: Set front = rear = 0 and store the element

Which pseudocode correctly deletes the first node of a non-empty singly linked list?

questions.question_text: If a doubly linked-list node q is inserted between p and r, which set of updates is required?

questions.option_c: It can loop indefinitely because temp never becomes NULL
